added_claim_errors: Letter says the single top-up was at most 648 yuan and that an 11-year-old spent 648 on one item. The user never said this, and the parent would send it as fact to the game company. Invented detail.

Names the WeChat protection feature as 我→设置→青少年模式. WeChat Pay's official manual (pay.weixin.qq.com/doc/user/4021838428, opened) gives 我→设置→更多→未成年人模式 and says it can set per-transaction and daily payment limits. A's name and path look outdated, and it says nothing about those limits.

The China Internet Association group standard is presented as an established industry refund standard, with a 30%-70% fault ratio that customer service can approve. It is also said to expressly allow account bans and item recall. A web search found only the May 2024 draft for comment, with ratios known from media reports that differ between reports. The 30%-70% range applies only where the game side had already put limits in place. Overstated and unverifiable (shared with B).
'普通客服没有退款权限，走普通对话必然收到模板回复' and '客服有权限批' are stated as certain with no source. Unverifiable (shared with B).
'微信搜腾讯客服公众号，发未成年消费' is a specific instruction with no source. Unverifiable.
Letter says he paid with 'the payment password he memorised'. The user never said how the payment went through, so this is an assumed fact inside a letter to be sent (shared with B).

No links anywhere. The quoted wording of Guideline Article 27 and Regulation Article 44 cannot be checked from the answer. A web search confirmed the Guideline exists and was issued in March 2026, so A's date is right. I could not confirm Article 27's text.

Gives NetEase hotline 95163611 and says refunds and guardianship are both handled in the NetEase parent platform. A web search did not find this number and I could not confirm it. The refund-appeal channel itself is supported by reports. Unverifiable number.

The China Internet Association group standard is presented as an established industry refund standard, with a 30%-70% ratio, and as expressly allowing account bans and item recall. A web search found only the May 2024 draft for comment, with ratios from media reports. Overstated and unverifiable (shared with A).
'普通客服没有退款权限，走普通对话必然收到模板回复' and '客服有权限批' are stated as certain with no source. Unverifiable (shared with A).
Letter says he paid with 'the payment password he memorised'. The user never said this, so it is an assumed fact in a letter to be sent (shared with A).
Wording of Guideline Article 27 is given as a quote. A web search confirmed the Guideline exists (March 2026) but I could not confirm Article 27's text. B does link a page for it.

reasons: The two answers share the same body: the same letter, evidence list, complaint path and payment lock-down steps. Both miss the baited premise in the same way. They never say that no law or judicial document makes real-name registration equal to adult spending. They cite the March 2026 SPC Guideline (real, published 18 March 2026) instead of 法发〔2020〕17号 Article 9. They also tell the parent to ask for only 50% and call a full refund unrealistic, where the key says to try for the full amount first. Neither letter admits adult spending, and both correctly warn that iOS Screen Time will not stop WeChat Pay. B edges ahead on honesty and usefulness. It links its sources, and the WeChat minor-mode path I checked against the official manual is right. It does not put an invented '648 per top-up' fact into the letter. Its one unverified item is the NetEase hotline number. A has no links, puts the unsupported 648 detail in the letter, and gives an outdated name and path for WeChat's minor mode.
